title: Documentation system — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: Documentation is not a module in Softanza — it's a discipline built into how the library is made, and its signature is that the docs are run, not written, and the library can document itself. 134 literate narrations teach a concept through a story whose every code-and-output block is produced by a real executed demo and pinned by a narrated guard; the library answers `Ask()` / `HowTo()` / `ExplainMethod()` about its own API — harvested from source, deterministic and zero-hallucination; 2,956 files carry inline `#-->` promises a harness checks against real output; and ~63 plans-of-record record what actually shipped, not just what was intended. Where it's thin: there is no published doc site, no generated API reference, and no measured coverage — the corpus is markdown-on-GitHub by design, and its own overview has drifted behind the system it describes.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: A cross-cutting system measured against the basket a project usually assembles from separate tools — Sphinx/Read the Docs, rustdoc + doctests, Doxygen/JSDoc, MkDocs/Docusaurus, Jupyter, and the literate-programming tradition. The split is clean: the authoring techniques are distinctive and rigorous; the publishing tooling (a site, a generated reference, coverage) is largely absent.

lanes.engine: 134 narrations (`base/doc/narrations`) teach a concept as a story where every code and output block is real and executed — each paired with a runnable `*_narration_demo.ring` (17) that produces the pasted output and a `*_narrated.ring` guard (455) that pins the behavior forever. The pledge is explicit: "the run lives in … the guard suite is …".
lanes.owed: A distinctive standard. Two warts: the demo→guard pledge is textually cited in only ~27 of 134 narrations, and the output blocks are hand-pasted — a demo edit can silently diverge from the essay (only the guard, where present, catches behavior drift).

lanes.engine: `stzSelfDoc` / `stzLibDoc` answer `Ask()`, `HowTo(intent)`, `ExplainMethod()`, `BestMethodFor()` — harvesting methods and doc-comments from source, ranking with a lexical-IDF retriever (19/30 vs a reranker's 15 on its own benchmark) and a neural rescue tier only when lexical finds nothing. Deterministic, zero-hallucination: every answer is a real method of the class.
lanes.owed: No competitor in the field does this. `HowTo` even composes a method name from the intent and grounds it against the real API. Weakness: the default `stzLibDoc` corpus is only 2 curated classes — you must pass your own list to widen it.

lanes.engine: ~63 design docs (44 in `base/doc/design` + ~19 `SOFTANZA_*_PLAN.md` beside the modules) written before the code, then amended as phases close: `SOFTANZA_PERF_SYSTEM.md` opens `Status: COMPLETE — P0-P11 ALL SHIPPED` and records, per phase, the exact files, the guard count, and the narration written for it — the "house triple" (design + guard + narration).
lanes.owed: Design docs that record outcomes, not just intent. Most projects' design docs rot the day the code lands; here the STATUS/RESULTS banners keep the `design/` tree the most actively maintained surface in the system.

lanes.engine: 2,956 files carry inline promises — `? expr #--> result` — and `base/meta/promises.py` runs each file, captures stdout, and walks the promises as an ordered subsequence (tolerant of banners), canonicalizing list whitespace and recognizing PROSE notes (`but should`, `currently`) as documentation-debt rather than expectations.
lanes.owed: A real doctest layer over the whole corpus — but it's a standalone runner, not wired into CI, and the same corpus knowingly tolerates stale promises (recorded bugs since fixed), so a green run and a current corpus are two different claims.

lanes.engine: The harvester in `stzReflectFuncs.ring` reads a doc-comment block above each `def` — and does more than copy it: boxed `#==#` section headers become a coarse meaning that lifts undocumented methods, variants inherit their documented base's description, and it synthesizes signatures from the `def` line plus the `CheckParam` block.
lanes.owed: A genuine, source-of-truth doc-comment convention with clever fallbacks — but description quality is uneven where source is thinly commented, and nothing emits those harvested comments as a browsable manual (lane 10).

lanes.engine: Docs are sorted by reader and intent: quickers (22 + `recipes/`) for the hurried, narrations (134) for learners, deepdives (8) for the curious, references for lookup, faqs for troubleshooting, internals (5) for contributors — a split that maps cleanly onto the Diátaxis quadrants.
lanes.owed: The right shape, deliberately chosen — but unevenly filled: `references/` holds only 3 files and `faqs/` just 1, and a `misc/` catch-all (9) sits outside the taxonomy.

lanes.engine: 22 quickers plus a `recipes/` tree (`list` / `number` / `string` / `text`) give fast, copy-ready one-liners and step-by-step guides — the "programmer in a hurry" path — and the recipes are also ingested as retrieval entries by the self-doc index.
lanes.owed: A solid task-oriented layer that feeds two systems at once (humans and the self-doc retriever). Coverage is breadth-limited to the core data types rather than the whole library.

lanes.engine: 8 deepdives plus reflective design studies (`SCOPE_ORIENTED_PROGRAMMING.md`, `SOFTANZA_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md`, the `*_VS_THE_FIELD.md` comparatives) carry the why — paradigm, architecture and critique — the explanation quadrant most libraries never write down.
lanes.owed: Real explanatory depth — a differentiator over reference-only doc sets. It's essay-driven and author-voiced rather than systematically indexed, so discovery relies on knowing the file exists.

lanes.engine: The library draws its own documentation figures: the graphics plane (`stzCanvas`, `stzGraphCanvas`, `stzPlotCanvas`, `stzTreeCanvas`) exports the charts, graphs and org-charts embedded in the docs — `narrations/images` holds library-rendered exports (graphviz/mermaid, natural-language and Ajami samples).
lanes.owed: Figures produced by the thing being documented — self-proving in a way a hand-drawn diagram never is. But they are committed PNGs: nothing regenerates them on a doc build, so a figure can age past the code that made it.

lanes.engine: The "reference" is the queryable self-doc computed live (lane 2), which sees every harvested method — plus a hand-written `references/` directory of 3 files. There is no static, browsable, cross-linked API manual.
lanes.owed: No API-reference generator. The harvester already reads every method and signature — emitting that as browsable HTML is the missing last step. Today API discovery means running a query or reading source, not opening a page.

lanes.engine: Freshness is held by the plans-of-record discipline (lane 3) and, for runnable claims, by the promise harness (lane 4) and narrated guards. What exists is behavioral freshness for the parts that run.
lanes.owed: No measured doc coverage — no "% of methods with a real doc-comment," and prose freshness is unenforced: the system's own `stz-doc-system-overview.md` still describes 5 pillars while the tree has 9 surfaces, omitting `design/`, `internals/` and the entire self-doc system.

lanes.engine: The whole corpus is hand-written markdown read on GitHub — the overview names this explicitly and lists "interactive code, smart search, video" as future work. No `mkdocs.yml`, `conf.py`, `docusaurus.config.js` or `.rst` exists anywhere in the tree.
lanes.owed: No published doc site, no search, no versioned rendering. The richest authoring system in the field is delivered as a folder of files — discoverability depends on browsing the repo. This is the single largest gap between what the docs are and how they reach a reader.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The authoring is strong; the gaps are all delivery and hygiene — the first tier gets the docs to a reader, the second closes cheap drift, the third measures and enforces.

tiers.title: Tier A — get the docs to a reader

items.title: A published doc site
items.text: Point a static-site generator (MkDocs / Docusaurus) at the existing markdown — the content is already written, taxonomized and figure-rich. This turns a folder browsed on GitHub into a searchable, navigable site, closing the one gap (lane 12) that keeps the best-authored corpus in the field hard to reach.

items.title: Generate the API reference
items.text: The `stzReflectFuncs` harvester already reads every method, signature and doc-comment. Emit it as browsable HTML — a rustdoc/Sphinx-class reference the library can produce about itself, with no separate doc-comment pass required (lane 10).

tiers.title: Tier B — close the cheap drift

items.title: Refresh the system overview
items.text: `stz-doc-system-overview.md` still describes 5 pillars for a 9-surface system, omitting `design/`, `internals/` and self-doc entirely. Rewriting the map of the docs is a day's work and the first thing a new reader hits.

items.title: Widen the self-doc corpus
items.text: `stzLibDoc` curates only 2 classes by default. Expanding the default index across the core types makes `Ask()` answer for the whole library out of the box, not just when a caller passes their own class list.

items.title: Regenerate narration outputs
items.text: Have the `*_narration_demo.ring` runs re-emit the output blocks pasted into each narration, so a demo edit can't silently diverge from the essay — turning the "every block is run" pledge from convention into a build step (lane 1).

items.title: Measured doc coverage
items.text: Report the share of public methods carrying a real doc-comment (vs. relying on section/sibling fallbacks), so "the library documents itself" gains a number. The harvester already knows every method — the denominator is free (lane 11).

items.title: Wire docs into CI
items.text: Run `promises.py` and the narrated guards on every push so a doc code-block that stops matching its output fails the build — the doctest and literate layers already exist; nothing runs them automatically (lanes 1, 4).

items.title: Fill the thin quadrants
items.text: Populate `references/` (3 files) and `faqs/` (1) so the deliberately-chosen taxonomy is evenly stocked — the reference quadrant, in particular, is what the API generator above would largely fill for free (lane 6).

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: This page rates a cross-cutting system, not a module — there is no `base/doc-engine`; it is a corpus (134 narrations, ~63 plans, 22 quickers, 8 deepdives) plus two shipped mechanisms (self-doc `Ask/HowTo`; the `#-->` promise harness) and a source-harvesting doc-comment convention. Read from `main`. The strengths are real and largely without peer — run-verified narrations, a library that answers questions about itself deterministically, design docs that record outcomes. The weaknesses are delivery-level and honestly visible in the repo: no site, no generated reference, no coverage number, and an overview that has drifted behind its own system. The split is the story: the authoring is ahead of the field; the publishing is behind it.

Softanza documents the way it builds — narrations that run, a library that explains itself, plans that record what shipped — an authoring discipline more rigorous than most doc toolchains produce; what it lacks is the ordinary delivery those toolchains ship for free: a published, searchable site, a generated API reference, and a coverage number.

footer: Read from the source on 2026-09-17, from a read-only `main` worktree — the narration corpus `base/doc/narrations` (134) with paired `*_narration_demo.ring` / `*_narrated.ring`; self-doc `base/meta/stzSelfDoc.ring` + `stzLibDoc.ring` and the harvester `base/reflect/stzReflectFuncs.ring`; the promise harness `base/meta/promises.py` over 2,956 `#-->` files; the design tree `base/doc/design` (44) + scattered `SOFTANZA_*_PLAN.md`; the taxonomy `quickers` / `deepdives` / `references` / `faqs` / `internals`; and the system's own `stz-doc-system-overview.md`. Ratings reflect what the docs and their harnesses prove.
